claim: GST-Atg19 directly interacts with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex in pull down experiments.
source: in pull down experiments GST-Atg19 used as a bait successfully pulled down Atg12~Atg5-Atg16, demonstrating a direct interaction between these two components (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A demonstrating pull-down results.

claim: Atg12~Atg5-Atg16-mCherry is robustly and specifically recruited to beads coated with GST-Atg19 under equilibrium conditions.
source: Atg12~Atg5-Atg16-mCherry was robustly and specifically recruited to these beads (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1B demonstrating recruitment of the complex to beads.

claim: The Atg34 cargo receptor interacts with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex.
source: The α-mannosidase (Ams1) receptor Atg34 was also able to bind the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex (Figure 1C)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C demonstrating binding of Atg34 to the complex.

claim: The interaction of cargo receptors with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex is a general property of cargo receptors.
source: The α-mannosidase (Ams1) receptor Atg34 was also able to bind the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex (Figure 1C), suggesting that this interaction is a more general property of cargo receptors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that multiple cargo receptors (Atg19 and Atg34) interact with the complex.

claim: Atg19 interacts with Atg5-TAP in S. cerevisiae cells.
source: In order to test if this interaction occurs in cells we performed immunoprecipitation experiments using Atg5-TAP to pull down 6xmyc-Atg19 (Figure 1D). Atg19 was specifically pulled down by Atg5-TAP.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Atg19 and the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex are in close proximity in living cells.
source: Employing the M-Track assay, which is based on the methylation of the human histone 3 N-terminus by the human SUV39H1 methyltransferase when the two components come into close contact (Brezovich et al., 2015; Zuzuarregui et al., 2012), we confirmed that Atg19 and the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex are in close proximity in living cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by M-Track assay data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Overexpression of a methyltransferase does not result in unspecific methylation of the histone 3 N-terminus.
source: It was previously shown that overexpression of a methyltransferase does not result in unspecific methylation of the histone 3 N-terminus (Brezovich et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Human GFP-ATG5 co-precipitates with mCherry-p62 in HeLa cells.
source: To this end, we co-expressed human GFP-ATG5 and mCherry-p62 in HeLa cells in which the endogenous p62 had been knocked-down by RNAi. mCherry-p62 was efficiently co-precipitated by GFP-ATG5 (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: mCherry-p62 is recruited to GFP-ATG5 coated beads in HeLa cell lysates.
source: We confirmed this result by using a microscopy-based assay in which we imaged the recruitment of mCherry-p62 to GFP-ATG5 coated beads in HeLa cell lysates (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: NDP52 is pulled down by GFP-ATG5.
source: We extended this analysis by investigating other human cargo receptors and found that NDP52 was also pulled down by GFP-ATG5 (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by pull-down data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Optineurin (OPTN) shows weak but consistent co-precipitation with GFP-ATG5.
source: In addition, we detected a weak but consistent co-precipitation of Optineurin (OPTN) (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-precipitation data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The S. cerevisiae Atg19 and Atg34 cargo receptors directly interact with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 E3-like enzyme.
source: In summary, the S. cerevisiae Atg19 and Atg34 cargo receptors directly interact with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 E3-like enzyme and an interaction with this complex is also detectable for the human cargo receptors p62, OPTN and NDP52.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: An interaction with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex is detectable for the human cargo receptors p62, OPTN and NDP52.
source: In summary, the S. cerevisiae Atg19 and Atg34 cargo receptors directly interact with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 E3-like enzyme and an interaction with this complex is also detectable for the human cargo receptors p62, OPTN and NDP52.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Atg5 is sufficient for binding to Atg19.
source: All proteins tested showed interaction with Atg19 suggesting that Atg5 is sufficient for the binding to Atg19 (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by pull-down data shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: A fraction of Atg5-Atg16 (1–46) shifts to higher molecular weight fractions in the presence of Atg19 in size exclusion chromatography experiments.
source: We confirmed this result in size exclusion chromatography experiments using Atg5-Atg16 (1–46) and Atg19. Indeed, a fraction of Atg5-Atg16 (1–46) shifted to higher molecular weight fractions in the presence of Atg19 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by size exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The presence of Atg16 has a stimulatory effect on the interaction of Atg5 with Atg19.
source: The presence of Atg16 had a stimulatory effect on the interaction of Atg5 with Atg19 suggesting that Atg16 could directly interact with Atg19 (Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by pull-down data shown in Figure 2A, 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Atg16 does not show detectable binding to Atg19 when tested in isolation.
source: However, when tested in isolation Atg16 did not show any detectable binding to Atg19 (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by pull-down data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Full length Atg16 may enhance the interaction of Atg5 with Atg19 by an allosteric effect on Atg5 or by increasing the avidity of the interaction due to its ability to self-associate.
source: Full length Atg16 may therefore enhance the interaction by an allosteric effect on Atg5 or by increasing the avidity of the interaction due to its ability to self-associate (Fujioka et al., 2010; Kaufmann et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is speculative and based on inference from the data and citations to previous work.

claim: Atg5 and Atg5-Atg16 show robust interaction with all Atg19 truncations including the C-terminal domain encompassing amino acids 365–415.
source: Atg5 and Atg5-Atg16 showed robust interaction with all Atg19 truncations including the C-terminal domain encompassing amino acids 365–415 (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by pull-down data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The presence of Atg12 changes the properties of the interaction of Atg5 with Atg19 and requires the presence of amino acids 124–254 of Atg19.
source: The presence of Atg12, either in context of the Atg12~Atg5 conjugate or the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex, changed the properties of the interaction and required the presence of amino acids 124–254, which include the cargo binding domain of Atg19 (Yamasaki et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by pull-down data and a citation to previous work.

claim: The coiled-coil domain of Atg19 is required for the interaction with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex when Atg5 is conjugated to Atg12.
source: This assay confirmed that the coiled-coil domain of Atg19 is required for the interaction when Atg5 is conjugated to Atg12 (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy-based interaction data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Deletion of the last eight amino acids containing the canonical AIM motif from the C-terminus of Atg19 strongly reduces the interaction with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex.
source: Intriguingly, deletion of the last eight amino acids containing the canonical AIM motif (Noda et al., 2008; Sawa-Makarska et al., 2014) from the C-terminus of Atg19 strongly reduced the interaction (Figure 3A)
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy-based interaction data shown in Figure 3A and citations to previous work.

claim: The canonical AIM motif in the extreme C-terminus of Atg19 contributes to the interaction with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex.
source: Intriguingly, deletion of the last eight amino acids containing the canonical AIM motif (Noda et al., 2008; Sawa-Makarska et al., 2014) from the C-terminus of Atg19 strongly reduced the interaction (Figure 3A) suggesting that this AIM motif contributes to the interaction of Atg19 with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that deletion of the AIM motif reduces the interaction.

claim: Deletion of the canonical AIM motif in the extreme C-terminus of Atg19 results in strong but incomplete reduction in Atg5 binding.
source: While deletion of the canonical AIM motif in the extreme C-terminus resulted in strong but incomplete reduction in Atg5 binding, further mutation of two additional AIM-like sequences (Abert et al., 2016; Sawa-Makarska et al., 2014) completely abolished the interaction (Figure 3B and Figure 3C Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy-based interaction data shown in Figure 3B, 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and citations to previous work.

claim: Mutation of two additional AIM-like sequences in Atg19 completely abolishes the interaction with Atg5.
source: While deletion of the canonical AIM motif in the extreme C-terminus resulted in strong but incomplete reduction in Atg5 binding, further mutation of two additional AIM-like sequences (Abert et al., 2016; Sawa-Makarska et al., 2014) completely abolished the interaction (Figure 3B and Figure 3C Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy-based interaction data shown in Figure 3B, 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and citations to previous work.

claim: The AIM-dependent association of Atg19 with Atg5 is relevant for the interaction of the two proteins in vivo.
source: The AIM-dependent association of Atg19 with Atg5 is relevant for the interaction of the two proteins in vivo as the W412A mutation in the canonical AIM motif of Atg19 results in markedly reduced interaction of the two proteins in co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The W412A mutation in the canonical AIM motif of Atg19 results in markedly reduced interaction with Atg5 in co-immunoprecipitation experiments.
source: The AIM-dependent association of Atg19 with Atg5 is relevant for the interaction of the two proteins in vivo as the W412A mutation in the canonical AIM motif of Atg19 results in markedly reduced interaction of the two proteins in co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The interaction of Atg5 with the C-terminus of Atg19 is AIM-dependent.
source: Thus, the interaction of Atg5 with the C-terminus of Atg19 is AIM-dependent and mutually exclusive with Atg8 binding.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that Atg8 outcompetes Atg5 binding to Atg19.

claim: The interaction of Atg5 with the C-terminus of Atg19 is mutually exclusive with Atg8 binding.
source: Thus, the interaction of Atg5 with the C-terminus of Atg19 is AIM-dependent and mutually exclusive with Atg8 binding.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that Atg8 outcompetes Atg5 binding to Atg19.

claim: Atg8 outcompetes Atg19-bound Atg5-mCherry-Atg16 (1–46) in a dose dependent manner.
source: Indeed, Atg8 outcompeted the Atg19-bound Atg5-mCherry-Atg16 (1–46) in a dose dependent manner. The loss of the Atg5-mCherry signal correlated with an increased GFP-Atg8 signal at the bead (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3E and 3F.

claim: The loss of the Atg5-mCherry signal correlates with an increased GFP-Atg8 signal at the bead.
source: Indeed, Atg8 outcompeted the Atg19-bound Atg5-mCherry-Atg16 (1–46) in a dose dependent manner. The loss of the Atg5-mCherry signal correlated with an increased GFP-Atg8 signal at the bead (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3E and 3F.

claim: Atg19 robustly recruits to cargo mimetic beads generated by attaching the prApe1 propeptide to them via a GST-tag.
source: First, we generated cargo mimetic beads by attaching the prApe1 propeptide to them via a GST-tag. Consistent with previous results Atg19 was robustly recruited to these beads (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A) (Pfaffenwimmer et al., 2014; Sawa-Makarska et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and citations to previous work.

claim: Atg19 recruits the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex to artificial cargo.
source: Next we tested if Atg19 recruited the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex to the artificial cargo. Indeed, the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex showed a strong Atg19 dependent signal at the beads (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex is displaced from cargo mimetic beads by GFP-Atg8 in a concentration dependent manner.
source: Employing this experimental setup, we then went on by adding GFP-Atg8 to the cargo mimetic beads (Figure 3G). The complex was displaced in a concentration dependent manner confirming that Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 and Atg8 compete for the same binding sites on Atg19.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 and Atg8 compete for the same binding sites on Atg19.
source: Employing this experimental setup, we then went on by adding GFP-Atg8 to the cargo mimetic beads (Figure 3G). The complex was displaced in a concentration dependent manner confirming that Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 and Atg8 compete for the same binding sites on Atg19.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that Atg8 displaces the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex from Atg19.

claim: The AIM motifs in Atg19 directly interact with Atg5.
source: The Atg5 subunit of the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex and the AIM-like motifs in Atg19 are both essential for the binding of these two components. Moreover, the interaction of Atg19 with Atg5 and Atg8 is mutually exclusive, strongly suggesting that the AIM motifs in Atg19 directly interact with Atg5.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that AIM motifs are essential for binding and the interaction is mutually exclusive with Atg8.

claim: Computational modeling and molecular dynamics simulations identified three possible binding sites for the canonical AIM motif peptide (411TWEEL415) of Atg19, two of which mapped to Atg5.
source: To identify potential binding sites in Atg5 for the AIM motif we employed computational modeling and molecular dynamics simulations. To this end, we used the structure of Atg5-Atg16 (1–46) from S. cerevisiae (PDB:2DYO) (Matsushita et al., 2007) and performed molecular dynamics simulations which allowed us to capture the flexibility of the Atg5-Atg16 (1–46) complex. Subsequently, in silico docking was performed for 10 randomly selected snapshots from the molecular dynamics trajectory using a peptide encompassing the canonical AIM motif (411TWEEL415) of Atg19. Modelling analysis suggested three possible binding sites for the peptide, two of which mapped to Atg5 (Figure 4A,B) and one to a site formed by Atg16.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling and molecular dynamics simulations, and citations to previous work.

claim: The two AIM binding sites in Atg5 contain residues K57 and K137 in the first binding site and N84 and R208 in the second binding site.
source: The other two sites were analyzed. Both contained residues that were persistently involved in forming salt bridges and/or hydrogen bonds with the TWEEL peptide. These were K57 and K137 in the first binding site (Figure 4A, pose 1) and N84 and R208 in the second binding site (Figure 4A, pose 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling and molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: The two AIM binding sites in Atg5 show a similar architecture composed of a hydrophobic pocket surrounded by positively charged residues.
source: These two sites show a similar architecture composed of a hydrophobic pocket surrounded by positively charged residues.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling and molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: The hydrophobic pocket in the AIM binding sites of Atg5 serves to dock W412 and L415 of the TWEEL peptide.
source: Specifically, molecular dynamics simulations showed that the hydrophobic pocket serves to dock W412 and L415 of the TWEEL peptide, while lysine, arginine and asparagine residues on the surface of Atg5 contact the peptide via salt bridges and hydrogen bonds with the glutamic acid residues E413 and E414.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling and molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: Lysine, arginine and asparagine residues on the surface of Atg5 contact the TWEEL peptide via salt bridges and hydrogen bonds with the glutamic acid residues E413 and E414.
source: Specifically, molecular dynamics simulations showed that the hydrophobic pocket serves to dock W412 and L415 of the TWEEL peptide, while lysine, arginine and asparagine residues on the surface of Atg5 contact the peptide via salt bridges and hydrogen bonds with the glutamic acid residues E413 and E414.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling and molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: The two AIM binding sites in Atg5 are unrelated to the AIM-binding sites of Atg8.
source: Structural superposition showed that the two sites are unrelated to the AIM-binding sites of Atg8 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural superposition analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Introduction of the K57E mutation into Atg5 results in strongly reduced recruitment of the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex to cargo mimetic beads.
source: Introduction of the K57E into Atg5 resulted in a strongly reduced recruitment of the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex, while the N84E mutation rendered the recruitment undetectable (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: The N84E mutation in Atg5 renders the recruitment of the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex to cargo mimetic beads undetectable.
source: Introduction of the K57E into Atg5 resulted in a strongly reduced recruitment of the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex, while the N84E mutation rendered the recruitment undetectable (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: The K57E,N84E double mutation in Atg5 results in loss of Atg12~Atg5-Atg16-mCherry complex recruitment to cargo mimetic beads.
source: When combined, the two mutations also resulted in a loss of Atg12~Atg5-Atg16-mCherry complex recruitment to the beads.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data.

claim: Residues K57 and N84 in Atg5 are likely to be directly involved in the formation of binding sites for the AIM motif.
source: Thus, introducing negative charge at positions 57 and 84 in the two predicted AIM binding sites interfered with the interaction of the two proteins. These residues are therefore likely to be directly involved in the formation of binding sites for the AIM motif.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that mutations at these positions interfere with the interaction.

claim: In the context of the Atg12~Atg5 conjugate, N84 in pose two would be largely covered by Atg12.
source: Interestingly, in the context of the Atg12~Atg5 conjugate N84 in pose two would be largely covered by Atg12 (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The coiled-coil domain of Atg19 may reorient Atg12 away from pose 2 to allow interaction with the C-terminal domain of Atg19.
source: This may explain why the C-terminal domain of Atg19 containing the AIM motif is not sufficient for the interaction with Atg12~Atg5 and requires the coiled-coil domain (Figure 2D–G), which may reorient Atg12 away from pose 2.
evidence: The claim is speculative and based on inference from structural and experimental data.

claim: The K57E and N84E mutations in Atg5 do not abolish the conjugation of Atg5 to Atg12.
source: The K57 and N84 mutations did not abolish the conjugation of Atg5 to Atg12 (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The K57E and N84E mutations in Atg5 do not cause significant defects in liposome binding of the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex.
source: We also did not observe significant defects of the mutant Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complexes with respect to liposome binding (Figure 5D)
evidence: The claim is supported by liposome co-sedimentation assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The K57E and N84E mutations in Atg5 do not cause significant defects in promoting Atg8 lipidation.
source: or of the single and double mutant Atg12~Atg5 conjugates with respect to promoting Atg8 lipidation (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by Atg8 conjugation assay data shown in Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The K57E,N84E double mutant Atg5 shows strongly reduced ability to interact with Atg19 in vivo.
source: Consistent with the results shown above (Figure 3D), wild type Atg5 robustly co-precipitated Atg19. The K57E,N84E double mutant Atg5 showed a strongly reduced ability to interact with Atg19, but the interaction was still detectable (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Atg16 interacts with Atg21 and this interaction recruits the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex to the pre-autophagosomal structure (PAS).
source: It was previously shown that Atg16 interacts with Atg21 and that this interaction recruits the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex to the pre-autophagosomal structure (PAS) (Juris et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The E102A mutation in Atg16 abolishes the Atg16 - Atg21 interaction.
source: To this end, we introduced the E102A mutation into Atg16, which was reported to abolish the Atg16 - Atg21 interaction (Juris et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The interaction of the Atg5 K57E,N84E mutant with Atg19 becomes undetectable in context of the Atg16 E102A mutation.
source: Indeed, the interaction of the Atg5 K57E,N84E with Atg19 became undetectable in context of the Atg16 E102A mutation (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The N84E mutation in Atg5 affects prApe1 processing more pronouncedly compared to the K57E mutation.
source: The N84E mutation, which had the stronger effect on the Atg19 - Atg5 interaction also affected prApe1 processing more pronouncedly compared to the K57E mutation while the K57E,N84E double mutation had the strongest effect on prApe1 processing (Figure 5G,H and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by prApe1 processing assay data shown in Figure 5G, 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The K57E,N84E double mutation in Atg5 has the strongest effect on prApe1 processing.
source: The N84E mutation, which had the stronger effect on the Atg19 - Atg5 interaction also affected prApe1 processing more pronouncedly compared to the K57E mutation while the K57E,N84E double mutation had the strongest effect on prApe1 processing (Figure 5G,H and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by prApe1 processing assay data shown in Figure 5G, 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: prApe1 processing is affected by the K57E,N84E double mutation in Atg5 under starvation condition in the context of the Atg16 D101A, E102A mutation.
source: prApe1 processing was also affected by the K57E,N84E double mutation under starvation condition in the context of the Atg16 D101A, E102A mutation (Figure 5—figure supplement 3 Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by prApe1 processing assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3 and Figure 5H.

claim: Starvation-induced bulk autophagy as measured by GFP-Atg8 cleavage is not significantly affected by the Atg5 K57E,N84E double mutation.
source: In contrast, starvation-induced bulk autophagy as measured by GFP-Atg8 cleavage and the Pho8∆60 assay was not significantly affected by the Atg5 K57E,N84E double mutation (Figure 5I,J), even when tested in combination with the Atg16 D101A, E102A mutant (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by GFP-Atg8 cleavage assay data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Starvation-induced bulk autophagy as measured by the Pho8∆60 assay is not significantly affected by the Atg5 K57E,N84E double mutation.
source: In contrast, starvation-induced bulk autophagy as measured by GFP-Atg8 cleavage and the Pho8∆60 assay was not significantly affected by the Atg5 K57E,N84E double mutation (Figure 5I,J), even when tested in combination with the Atg16 D101A, E102A mutant (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pho8∆60 assay data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: The Atg19 cargo receptor can recruit the E3-like Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex to the prApe1 cargo.
source: The data presented so far have shown that the Atg19 cargo receptor can recruit the E3-like Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex to the prApe1 cargo and that mutations that abolish this interaction reduce the efficiency of the Cvt pathway.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mutations that abolish the interaction of Atg19 with the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex reduce the efficiency of the Cvt pathway.
source: The data presented so far have shown that the Atg19 cargo receptor can recruit the E3-like Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex to the prApe1 cargo and that mutations that abolish this interaction reduce the efficiency of the Cvt pathway.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The cargo receptor - E3 interaction might be a minimal axis to couple Atg8 conjugation to the cargo.
source: The cargo receptor - E3 interaction might therefore be a minimal axis to couple Atg8 conjugation to the cargo.
evidence: The claim is speculative and based on inference from the data.

claim: Small unilamellar vesicles (SUVs) are recruited to Atg19-bound cargo mimetic beads in an Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex dependent manner.
source: To test this, we added small unilamellar vesicles (SUVs) labeled by the incorporation of ATTO390-PE or Rhodamine to Atg19-bound cargo mimetic beads in the presence or absence of the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1). The SUVs were recruited to the beads in an Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex dependent manner (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex brings the membrane substrate for Atg8 conjugation in proximity of the cargo.
source: Thus, the complex brings the membrane substrate for Atg8 conjugation in proximity of the cargo.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that SUVs are recruited to cargo mimetic beads in an Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex dependent manner.

claim: GFP-Atg8 shows increased signal at the cargo in the presence of ATP in a reconstituted system.
source: Next we analyzed if this minimal system would allow local accumulation of conjugated Atg8 by adding the ubiquitin-like molecule GFP-Atg8, the E1-like enzyme Atg7, the E2-like enzyme Atg3, and the cofactors MgCl2 and ATP to the system. Intriguingly, GFP-Atg8 showed increased signal at the cargo in the presence of ATP (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The presence of ATP increases the signal for the membrane and the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex at the cargo.
source: We also detected an increased signal for the membrane and the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex (Figure 6A), likely due to its association with Atg8 and the membranes (Kaufmann et al., 2014; Romanov et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6A and citations to previous work.

claim: The increased GFP-Atg8 signal at the beads in the presence of ATP may be due to lipidation of Atg8 and thus its stable anchoring and concentration on the membranes.
source: Since the presence of ATP increased the GFP-Atg8 signal at the beads, this effect may be due to lipidation of Atg8 and thus its stable anchoring and concentration on the membranes.
evidence: The claim is speculative and based on inference from the data.

claim: Lipidated Atg8 is more strongly bound by the Atg19 receptor.
source: If so, then the lipidated Atg8 should be more strongly bound by the Atg19 receptor (Abert et al., 2016; Sawa-Makarska et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on inference and citations to previous work.

claim: Atg8 recovers more slowly in the presence of ATP in FRAP experiments on cargo mimetic beads.
source: To test this, we conducted FRAP experiments on the cargo mimetic beads (Figure 6B). Indeed, Atg8 recovered more slowly in the presence of ATP and recovery was slowest for the Atg8 positive puncta, which we interpret as larger Atg8-positive vesicular structures (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Recovery of Atg8 is slowest for the Atg8 positive puncta, which are interpreted as larger Atg8-positive vesicular structures.
source: To test this, we conducted FRAP experiments on the cargo mimetic beads (Figure 6B). Indeed, Atg8 recovered more slowly in the presence of ATP and recovery was slowest for the Atg8 positive puncta, which we interpret as larger Atg8-positive vesicular structures (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 6B and interpretation by the authors.

claim: In the presence of ATP, the bead associated signal is increased after recruitment of vesicles to cargo mimetic beads and washing away unbound vesicles, consistent with local lipidation of Atg8 at the cargo.
source: For this reason, we recruited vesicles to cargo mimetic beads via the Atg12~Atg5-Atg16 complex and washed away unbound vesicles (Figure 6C). Subsequently, we added the Atg8 conjugation machinery. In the presence of ATP the bead associated signal was increased, consistent with local lipidation of Atg8 at the cargo (Figure 6C).
